title: First Recorded Drought
description: Spanish colonizers first document Lake Poopó's tendency to evaporate during drought periods.

title: Transition 'al Seco'
description: Uru communities begin their transition from lacustrine life to dry land, settling on previously Aymara-owned land.

title: Chholo Language Extinction
description: The Chholo language, spoken by the Urus of Lake Poopó, ceases to be actively spoken by the mid-20th century.

title: First Major El Niño
description: Strong El Niño event drastically reduces Lake Poopó's water levels for the first time in the modern era.

title: Severe El Niño Event
description: 1997-98 El Niño causes dramatic water loss. Aerial flamingo surveys count 120,000 birds.

title: Quinoa Boom Begins
description: Surging global demand for quinoa drives dramatic agricultural expansion across the altiplano, increasing water diversion.

title: Ramsar Designation
description: Lakes Poopó and Uru Uru designated as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance, recognizing extraordinary biodiversity.

title: Bolivia's New Constitution
description: Bolivia's 2009 Constitution enshrines indigenous peoples' rights to prior consultation before extractive activities.

title: Lake Poopó 'Disappears'
description: In December, the city of Oruro declares that Lake Poopó has disappeared. The event triggers global media attention.

title: Cooperativa de Artesanías
description: With a U.N. World Food Programme grant, Uru women form an artisan cooperative, centralizing craftsmaking as economic strategy.

title: Political Transition
description: Bolivia ends two decades of MAS governance. New center-right government embraces private mining investment, raising concerns for Uru communities.
